clue.text: Attendants like the sound of praises

indicators.note: the clue asks for a word that is said the same way as the synonym for praises

parts.note: paeans are songs of praise

explanation.surface: Servants who enjoy hearing themselves complimented.
explanation.walkthrough: PAEANS (songs of praise) and PEONS are pronounced alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A peon is a lowly servant or labourer, an attendant in India and Latin America.

clue.text: Expert gesture in advertising campaign

parts.note: a pro is an expert or professional
a motion is a movement or gesture of the hand

explanation.surface: A skilled sign used in marketing.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is a publicity drive to boost sales of a product.

clue.text: Attack — but not 19

parts.note: the answer to 19 across, meaning compensation

explanation.surface: An assault, but not a counterbalance.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 across is OFFSET; replacing OFF with its opposite ON gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the start of an assault, a charge against an enemy.

clue.text: Did stint as foot runner to journalist at Westminster

an MP sits in Parliament at Westminster
ed is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter who served a spell of duty at Parliament as a messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Did stint' suggests served a term, but stint means to be sparing.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to stint, to be mean with or give too little of something.

clue.text: Musical group hired after month ended

indicators.note: hired follows the month and ended, so its piece is placed last

parts.note: Sept is the abbreviation for September
up means over or finished, as in 'time's up'
let means rented out or hired

explanation.definitionFit: In music a septuplet is a group of seven notes played in the time of four or six.

clue.text: County officers

explanation.surface: Local council officials.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffs is the standard abbreviation for Staffordshire, a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation names an English Midlands shire; a military commander's aides form the general's staffs.

clue.text: Too much to request about a god

parts.note: a plea is an appeal or request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: It is excessive to petition a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or overabundance.

clue.text: Like head of Henley, has bachelor circle in celibate surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the celibate word encloses the other letters

parts.note: unwed means unmarried
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Henley's leader is a single man who stays among the chaste.

explanation.definitionFit: The poet's head in Invictus is not bent in defeat, i.e. defiant.

clue.text: Jack's on board Glorious, for the most part hard-working

indicators.note: on board means the sailor is set inside the ship's name
for the most part keeps nearly all of the ship's name, dropping one letter

parts.note: a jack or AB (able seaman) is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor on HMS Glorious is mostly industrious.
explanation.walkthrough: Glorious was a Royal Navy ship; drop its G to get LORIOUS, and AB goes in after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Laborious describes someone industrious and diligent, as well as a task needing great effort.

clue.text: Way to walk in this part of Tyre

explanation.surface: A path through this section of the ancient city of Tyre.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyre looks like the Lebanese city but is the British spelling of tire, the wheel's rubber casing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tread is a step or gait, and also the grooved surface of a wheel's rubber.

clue.text: Maybe 2, a bit stubborn

parts.note: the answer to 2 down, meaning attack
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Perhaps an attack is somewhat obstinate in character.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2 is a cross-reference to 2 down, ONSET; its letters with A and BIT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate is a direct synonym of headstrong and unyielding.

clue.text: "Starless and — black" (Thomas)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from the opening of Dylan Thomas's play Under Milk Wood, describing the night

explanation.walkthrough: Under Milk Wood opens 'To begin at the beginning: it is spring, moonless night in the small town, starless and ___-black'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes Dylan Thomas's compound adjective for the pitch-dark night in Under Milk Wood.

clue.text: Elated — unlike Atlas

explanation.surface: Overjoyed, in contrast with the Titan of myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Atlas in Greek myth bears the heavens (often shown as a globe) on his shoulders, so he is beneath it rather than above.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for euphoric, and literally describes standing above the globe rather than holding it up.

clue.text: They're battling without money in the interior

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is dropped from the battling teams

parts.note: opposing sides are those who fight each other

explanation.surface: Combatants with no funds are found deep inland.
explanation.walkthrough: S was the abbreviation for the shilling, a pre-decimal British coin; removing it from SIDES leaves SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The interior of something is its inner part, the part within.

clue.text: Smart cane broken at wedding for instance

indicators.note: broken means the words are smashed and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elegant walking stick snaps during the marriage ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage is one of the seven sacraments of the Catholic Church, a holy rite.

clue.text: Nail to cross in Yorkshire

parts.note: a brad is a thin flat nail with a small head
to ford is to cross a river by wading

explanation.surface: A nail that must be got over somewhere in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Bradford is a city in West Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to a place located in that northern English county.

clue.text: Railway fog signal heeded going up a hill

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: noted means heeded or paid attention to
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.definitionFit: Railway detonators are small explosive caps placed on the line that bang as a warning to drivers in fog.

clue.text: A French material on Orient a strip

cloth is fabric or material

clue.text: No act in church composition

indicators.note: in means the act sits inside the church abbreviation

clue.text: Rapid rise increases desire

parts.note: ups as a verb means raises or increases
an urge is a strong desire

clue.text: Compensation for not being shot

explanation.surface: Damages paid for not getting shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as 'off set': away from the film set, so not being filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: An offset is something that balances or makes up for a loss; off the set means away from where filming happens.

clue.text: Wildly excited at its rise in foreign currency

indicators.note: rise in a down clue reads the word upward, back to front

parts.note: the word it, the possessive being ignored

explanation.definitionFit: Frantic means frenzied, distraught with excitement or worry.

clue.text: Show financiers pieces of gold

explanation.walkthrough: An angel was an old English gold coin, and theatre backers are called angels.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical investors are known as backers in the trade; the old English gold coin bore the archangel Michael.

clue.text: Initially Tom managed the place, accepting scheme for graft

clue.text: The gallery has a point that makes sense

explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, along with sight, hearing, smell and touch.

clue.text: In other words, tide's out

parts.note: the letters of the word tides, the apostrophe ignored

clue.text: Completely cut, say

clue.text: Course is ten metres roughly

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
